title: Fruit and Vegetable Smoothie, No Dairy

content.title: About
content.content: A fruit and vegetable smoothie without dairy is a beverage made from fresh fruits, vegetables, and plant‑based liquids (water, coconut water, plant milks). It contains no dairy ingredients, making it suitable for lactose‑intolerant individuals and vegans.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Smoothies retain most of the vitamins and minerals from the raw produce because they are not heat‑treated.
Adding leafy greens such as spinach or kale barely changes the taste but dramatically boosts nutritional value.
Acai and pomegranate blends are often marketed as “superfood” smoothies due to their high antioxidant content.
For a creamier texture, avocado or frozen bananas are used instead of dairy.
Smoothies can be stored in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours, though flavor and nutrient levels are best right after blending.

items.title: Rich in vitamins C and A
items.content: Fruits and vegetables like carrots, bell peppers, and citrus provide vitamin C and provitamin A, supporting immunity and vision.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber from the produce aids digestion, promotes satiety, and helps regulate blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: The absence of dairy keeps saturated fat low, which is beneficial for heart health.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: A large water component and electrolytes from coconut water help maintain fluid balance.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Berries (blueberry, raspberry) and leafy greens contain polyphenols that combat free radicals.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Using too many sweet fruits can raise the smoothie’s glycemic index, which may be undesirable for diabetics.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: Some add‑ins (nuts, chia seeds) can trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Digestive issues
items.content: A large amount of fiber in one serving may cause bloating or loose stools in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Metallic taste
items.content: Blending acidic ingredients (lemon, lime) in metal containers can cause slight oxidation, affecting flavor.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Drink the smoothie immediately after blending. It can also be poured into a bowl and topped with granola, nuts, seeds, or fresh berries. For a more filling version, add protein powder or rolled oats.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the prepared smoothie in an airtight container in the refrigerator for no more than 24 hours. For longer storage, portion it out and freeze; thaw in the fridge before drinking and give it a quick shake.
